full_text:
झारखंड में 18 सितंबर तक गरज के साथ बारिश के आसार, येलो अलर्ट जारी
रांची, 14 सितंबर (हि.स.)। झारखंड की राजधानी रांची सहित राज्य के विभिन्न हिस्सों में 18 सितंबर तक गरज के साथ हल्की बारिश होने और आकाशीय बिजली गिरने की संभावना है। मौसम विभाग ने इसे देखते हुए सोमवार को येलो अलर्ट जारी किया है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, दक्षिण-पूर्वी राजस्थान और उससे सटे गुजरात के क्षेत्र तथा दक्षिण-पश्चिमी मध्य प्रदेश और दक्षिण-पूर्वी राजस्थान के आसपास निम्न दबाव का क्षेत्र बना हुआ है। इससे संबंधित मौसम प्रणाली धीरे-धीरे देश के दक्षिणी हिस्से की ओर बढ़ रही है। इसके प्रभाव से आने वाले दिनों में झारखंड में भी बारिश और गरज-चमक की गतिविधियां बढ़ने की संभावना है।
पिछले 24 घंटों के दौरान राज्य में सबसे अधिक 55.2 मिलीमीटर बारिश दुमका के महारो में दर्ज की गई। इस दौरान पूर्वी सिंहभूम के बहरागोड़ा में राज्य का सबसे अधिक तापमान 35.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। वहीं, लातेहार में न्यूनतम तापमान 19.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस रिकॉर्ड किया गया।
रांची और आसपास के इलाकों में सोमवार सुबह मौसम साफ रहा, लेकिन दोपहर बाद आसमान में बादल छा गए। कुछ स्थानों पर हल्की बारिश भी दर्ज की गई। राजधानी में सोमवार को अधिकतम तापमान 30 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 22.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा।
मौसम विभाग के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, जमशेदपुर में अधिकतम तापमान 33.6 और न्यूनतम 25.6 डिग्री, डाल्टनगंज में 32.2 और 25.1 डिग्री, बोकारो में 32.1 और 26.1 डिग्री तथा चाईबासा में 33.4 और 23 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया।
विभाग ने बारिश के दौरान गरज और आकाशीय बिजली की आशंका को देखते हुए लोगों से सावधानी बरतने की अपील की है।

SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - It’ll be a quiet morning as we begin a new week across the Coastal Empire and Lowcountry.
Temperatures will be in the low to mid 70s at daybreak with dry roadways. We’ll warm to about 90 degrees by lunchtime, followed by highs in the mid 90s.
This will be our warmest afternoon out of the next week! Heat index values will reach the lower triple digits from early afternoon into the early evening. Widespread rain is not expected; one or two small showers could form along the coast around 3 PM. Calm weather returns this evening.
Monday Beach Forecast: It’ll be a warm day at the beach with heat index values as high as 105 degrees during the afternoon. Rain is not expected, and wave heights will range from 2 to 3 feet with a low risk for rip currents.
Tuesday will be the day we begin to transition back to our average temperatures. You won’t notice much of a difference in the morning, but afternoon high will be in the upper 80s. That’s after a few showers could move through during the morning and midday hours, but severe weather is not expected. The wind will pick up during the afternoon, with gusts of 25 to 30 miles per hour possible out of the east. Dry conditions and lighter winds will be around during the evening.
Our average low is about 70 degrees for this time of the year, which is where we should bottom out on Wednesday morning. We will briefly drop to the upper 60s at daybreak, enjoy! Drier air will also be filtering in, meaning even with highs in the mid to upper 80s, it won’t feel as muggy. A few wind gusts of 20 to 25 miles per hour will be possible through the afternoon. This will be one of our nicer days we have had in a while.
We’ll start out near 70 degrees again on Thursday morning followed by highs in the mid to upper 80s. We will once again have breezy conditions with gusts of 20 to 25 miles per hour possible. The difference on Thursday is that there is a slight chance for an isolated afternoon downpour or two.
We’ll keep a low-end rain chance on Friday with morning lows in the lower 70s and highs in the upper 80s. There will probably be a few more showers around compared to the previous few days. Scattered showers and storms will be possible both Saturday and Sunday afternoon with highs in the upper 80s.
Tropical update: The is an area of low pressure about 1,000 miles west of Bermuda that has a 30% chance of becoming a tropical depression over the next seven days. Separate from that system, Long-range models are hinting at the chance for a tropical depression to develop in the western Atlantic during the week of September 23rd to the 29th. There are no local concerns at this time, but it is important to remember that even though we had had a quiet season, it might not stay quiet!

full_text:
THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The India Meteorological Department warned of the possibility of heavy rainfall across the state. A 'Yellow Alert' was issued for four districts—Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, and Palakkad—for today. A Yellow Alert has also been issued for Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad districts for tomorrow. The current weather advisory remains in effect until Wednesday.
IMD predicted moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and winds reaching speeds of up to 40 km/h in isolated areas. The term 'heavy rainfall' refers to a situation where precipitation ranges from 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm within 24 hours.
